You are checking a piece of writing for patterns common in AI-generated text. You will get an ORIGINAL draft and a TEXT to check. Check only TEXT. Use ORIGINAL only to find claims TEXT adds.

Count every instance in TEXT of these patterns (from Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing"):

1. Not X but Y: "It's not just X, it's Y", "This doesn't mean X. It means Y.", a clipped negative tail such as ", no guessing".
2. One-line closers and dramatic fragments: a short line that restates the point ("That is the real win.", "Let that sink in."), a row of verbless fragments ("No fees. No catch.").
3. Sayings that sound deep: "At its core", "The real question is", "X is the language of Y".
4. Staged run-up: "Let's dive in", "Here's the thing", "Honestly?", "Here's what you need to know".
5. Arguing with no one: "This isn't about...", "I'm not saying...", "To be clear", a rejected option nobody raised.
6. Forced triads: three items or three parallel clauses where the meaning does not need three.
7. Repeated sentence openings for rhythm.
9. Stacked qualifiers: "could potentially", "might arguably".
12. Overused AI words: delve, tapestry, testament, showcase, pivotal, crucial, landscape (abstract), vibrant, intricate, underscore, highlight (verb), enhance, foster, seamless, robust (figurative), meticulous, additionally.
13. Inflated significance: "a pivotal moment", "stands as a testament", "the future looks bright", "a step in the right direction".
14. Vague connection: "associated with", "linked to" where the relationship is not named.
15. Shallow -ing riders: a clause such as ", highlighting...", ", ensuring...", ", reflecting..." tacked onto a fact.
16. Sales language: nestled, breathtaking, stunning, must-visit, renowned, magical, unforgettable, in the heart of.
17. Borrowed authority: "experts say", "studies show" with no named source.
18. Avoiding is/are/has: "serves as", "stands as", "boasts", "features".
19. Bold as decoration, or list items that each open with a bold label and a colon.
20. Decorative headings: Title Case Headings, emojis, arrows.
22. Chatbot residue: "I hope this helps", "Great question", "Let me know if".
23. Knowledge-limit disclaimers and guesses.
24. A heading repeated in the first sentence under it.
25. Writing about the document: "In this post we'll cover", "The table below shows".

Count each separate instance once, under its best-fitting pattern. A careful human writer would also use some of these; count them anyway. Do not count dashes or curly quotes.

We're thrilled to announce that shared budgets are coming to Ledgerly on **March 3**, giving small teams a powerful new way to plan, track, and manage finances together.

Until now, keeping everyone on the same page about team spending meant endless spreadsheet updates, Slack messages, and budget meetings that could have been emails. Everyone sees the same numbers at the same time, so there's no confusion about whether you can approve that software subscription or book those conference tickets.

We designed shared budgets with real team workflows in mind. Set spending limits by category, assign budget owners, and get notifications when you're approaching thresholds. Team members can log expenses as they happen, attach receipts, and add context so everyone understands the story behind the numbers.

Permission controls let you decide who can view, edit, or manage each budget. Give your whole team visibility while restricting editing to budget owners, or open everything up for full collaboration—it's your call.

Shared budgets are included with Ledgerly's Team plan at **$12 per seat per month**. There's no premium tier to unlock, no per-budget fees—just straightforward pricing that scales with your team.

Current Team plan subscribers will get access automatically on March 3. If you're on our free plan and want to try shared budgets, upgrading takes just a few clicks.

Shared budgets are just the beginning. We're already working on budget templates, automated expense categorization, and deeper integrations with the tools your team uses every day.

# Ridgeway Coffee Commits to Compostable Packaging Across All Retail Bags

We're excited to announce a major milestone in our sustainability journey: Ridgeway Coffee is transitioning all our retail coffee bags to 100% compostable packaging. This change represents our commitment to reducing environmental impact while continuing to deliver the exceptional coffee quality our customers expect.

Since founding Ridgeway Coffee in 2019, we've grown from a single location to 14 cafes across the region, shipping approximately 40,000 bags of coffee each year to homes and businesses. With that growth comes responsibility—responsibility to our customers, our community, and our planet. Traditional coffee packaging, while effective at preserving freshness, contributes to the mounting problem of plastic waste. We knew we could do better.

After extensive research and testing, we've partnered with leading sustainable packaging innovators to develop bags that maintain coffee freshness while breaking down naturally in commercial composting facilities. These new bags are made from plant-based materials that will fully decompose within 12-16 weeks, leaving no toxic residue behind.

This transition means that every one of those 40,000 bags we ship annually will have a dramatically reduced environmental footprint. Instead of sitting in landfills for decades, our packaging will return nutrients to the soil. For our customers, this means you can enjoy your morning brew knowing that every element—from bean to bag—reflects values of environmental stewardship.

The switch hasn't been without challenges. Compostable materials require different handling and storage protocols, and the investment is significant. But when we calculated the environmental cost of maintaining the status quo, the choice became clear. Our team across all 14 locations has embraced this change enthusiastically, and we're already exploring additional sustainability initiatives for our cafes.

We're grateful to our loyal customers who've supported us since 2019 and helped make this transition possible. Your choice to buy Ridgeway Coffee now carries even greater impact. Together, we're proving that exceptional coffee and environmental responsibility aren't mutually exclusive—they're essential partners in building a better future.

# How to Repot a Fiddle-Leaf Fig

Fiddle-leaf figs are stunning houseplants that require periodic repotting to maintain their health and vigor. Plan to repot your fiddle-leaf fig every 18 months to give the roots adequate space to grow and prevent the plant from becoming root-bound.

## When to Repot

Spring is the ideal time to repot your fiddle-leaf fig. During this season, the plant enters its active growth phase, allowing it to recover quickly from the stress of transplanting and establish itself in its new container.

## Choosing the Right Pot

Select a new pot that is 2 inches wider in diameter than the current one. This provides sufficient room for root growth without overwhelming the plant with too much soil, which can lead to waterlogging. Most importantly, ensure your chosen pot has drainage holes at the bottom. Proper drainage is essential for preventing root rot, one of the most common issues affecting fiddle-leaf figs.

## Step-by-Step Process

**Prepare your materials:** Gather your new pot, fresh well-draining potting mix (preferably formulated for indoor plants), and water.

**Remove the plant:** Gently tip the pot on its side and carefully slide the fiddle-leaf fig out. If it's stuck, run a knife around the inside edge or tap the pot's sides to loosen the root ball.

**Inspect the roots:** Check for any brown, mushy, or circling roots. Trim away damaged roots with clean scissors and gently tease apart circling roots to encourage outward growth.

**Add soil:** Place a layer of fresh potting mix in the bottom of the new pot, enough so that when you place the plant inside, the top of the root ball sits about an inch below the rim.

**Position and fill:** Center the plant in the new pot and fill around the sides with potting mix, pressing gently to eliminate air pockets. Leave the root crown at the same level it was in the previous pot.

**Water thoroughly:** Water the plant until liquid drains from the bottom holes, then place it in its usual spot with bright, indirect light.

Your fiddle-leaf fig should now thrive in its new home for the next 18 months.

# How to Repot a Fiddle-Leaf Fig

Fiddle-leaf figs are gorgeous, but they don't love being cramped. Plan on repotting yours about every 18 months so the roots have room to spread and the plant doesn't get root-bound.

## When to Repot

Do it in spring. The plant is just getting into its growing season then, so it bounces back from the shock faster and settles into the new pot.

## Choosing the Right Pot

Go up about 2 inches in diameter from the current pot. Any bigger and you've got a lot of extra soil sitting wet around the roots, which is how you end up with waterlogging. The one thing you can't skip is drainage holes in the bottom. Root rot is probably the most common way people kill these plants, and good drainage is your best defense.

## Step-by-Step Process

**Get your stuff together:** You'll need the new pot, fresh well-draining potting mix (one made for indoor plants is fine), and some water.

**Take the plant out:** Tip the pot onto its side and gently slide the fig out. If it's stuck, run a knife around the inside edge or tap the sides of the pot to loosen the root ball.

**Look at the roots:** You're checking for anything brown, mushy, or wrapped in circles. Snip off the damaged bits with clean scissors, and loosen up any circling roots with your fingers so they grow outward.

**Add some soil:** Put a layer of fresh mix in the bottom of the new pot. You want enough that the top of the root ball ends up about an inch below the rim.

**Set it in and fill:** Center the plant, then pack mix in around the sides, pressing lightly to push out air pockets. Keep the root crown at the same level it was in the old pot.

**Water well:** Keep watering until it runs out the bottom holes, then put it back in its usual spot with bright, indirect light.

That's it. Your fig should be happy in its new pot for the next 18 months or so.

Get ready, young readers! The Hollis Public Library is thrilled to announce the return of our beloved Summer Reading Challenge, kicking off on June 15 for eight weeks of literary adventure and fun.

# Kestrel 2 Running Shoe Review

After logging 300 miles in the Kestrel 2, I can confidently say this shoe has earned a permanent spot in my rotation. At $140, it sits in the sweet spot between budget trainers and premium models, and the performance more than justifies the price.

## Lightweight Without Compromise

The first thing you notice is the weight—or lack thereof. At 248 grams, the Kestrel 2 feels incredibly light on the foot without sacrificing durability. I was initially skeptical that such a lightweight trainer could handle high mileage, but three hundred miles later, the midsole still feels responsive and the outsole shows minimal wear.

## Versatile Performance

The 8 mm drop makes this shoe remarkably versatile. It's low enough to encourage good form and midfoot striking, but not so minimal that it demands perfect technique. I've used these for everything from easy recovery runs to tempo workouts, and they've handled every pace comfortably. The transition feels smooth and natural, whether I'm cruising at an easy 9-minute pace or pushing closer to 7-minute miles.

## Comfort and Fit

The upper strikes an excellent balance between breathability and structure. My feet stay cool on hot summer runs, but I never feel like I'm swimming in the shoe. The heel cup locks in securely without any slippage, and I haven't experienced any hot spots or blisters across all those miles—a testament to the thoughtful design.

## Room for Improvement

If I'm being critical, the cushioning is on the firmer side. Runners who prefer a plush, marshmallow-soft ride might find these a bit too responsive. I personally appreciate the ground feel, but it's worth considering if you have specific preferences.

## The Verdict

The Kestrel 2 punches well above its weight class. It's light, responsive, durable, and versatile enough to be a true daily trainer. For runners looking for a do-it-all shoe that won't break the bank, this is an excellent choice. I'm already eyeing a second pair for when these finally give out—which, at this rate, won't be anytime soon.

**Rating: 4.5/5**

# Heat Pumps: An Efficient Alternative to Traditional Heating

A heat pump is a heating and cooling system that works by transferring heat rather than generating it. Unlike furnaces that burn fuel to create warmth, heat pumps move existing heat from one place to another—extracting it from outdoor air in winter and reversing the process in summer to cool your home.

## How They Work

The technology might sound counterintuitive: pulling heat from cold outdoor air. But even at freezing temperatures, thermal energy exists in the air. Heat pumps use a refrigerant cycle and compressor to capture this energy and concentrate it indoors. Modern systems are remarkably effective, with many models operating efficiently down to -15°C (-5°F) or lower.

## Impressive Efficiency

The key advantage of heat pumps is their extraordinary efficiency. A quality heat pump delivers approximately 300% efficiency—meaning for every unit of electricity consumed, it produces three units of heat. This happens because the system moves heat rather than creating it. In contrast, even the best gas furnaces max out around 98% efficiency, converting nearly all their fuel to heat but never exceeding that 1:1 ratio.

## The Economics

Heat pumps represent a significant upfront investment, typically costing more than conventional HVAC systems. However, the long-term economics often favor heat pumps thanks to lower operating costs from that superior efficiency. The federal tax credit of up to $2,000 helps offset initial costs, and many states offer additional incentives.

With an expected lifespan of around 15 years, heat pumps provide long-term value. Your actual savings depend on local electricity and fuel prices, climate, and your home's insulation quality.

## Is It Worth It?

Heat pumps make the most financial sense if you're replacing an existing system, live in a moderate climate, or currently heat with expensive fuel oil or electric resistance heating. They're also compelling for anyone prioritizing environmental impact, as they dramatically reduce carbon emissions compared to fossil fuel systems.

For homes in extremely cold climates, a hybrid approach—pairing a heat pump with a backup heating source—may be optimal. Overall, heat pumps represent mature, proven technology that delivers both comfort and efficiency for most homeowners.

# How Fernhill Dental Cut Missed Appointments by 60% with Text Reminders

## The Challenge

Fernhill Dental, a family practice operating two clinics in suburban Portland, faced a persistent problem that plagued their operations and bottom line: missed appointments. With no-show rates hovering around 18%, the practice was losing nearly one in five appointment slots. This translated to wasted chair time, frustrated staff constantly calling to fill gaps, and reduced revenue that made it harder to serve their growing patient base.

"Every empty chair is a patient we could have helped," says Dr. Sarah Chen, Fernhill's managing partner. "But more than that, we had patients who genuinely needed care waiting weeks for openings while slots sat unused because someone simply forgot."

The practice had tried reminder phone calls, but reaching patients during business hours proved difficult. Many calls went to voicemail, and staff spent hours each day leaving messages that patients might never hear.

## The Solution

Fernhill implemented an automated text reminder system that sent appointment confirmations and reminders to patients via SMS. The solution required minimal setup—patients could opt in by providing their mobile number, and the system integrated seamlessly with their existing practice management software.

Patients received a confirmation immediately after booking, followed by reminders three days and 24 hours before their appointment. The texts included the appointment date, time, location, and a simple option to confirm or reschedule with a reply.

## The Results

Within three months, no-show rates across both Fernhill clinics dropped from 18% to 7%—a 60% reduction. The impact was immediate and measurable. Chair utilization improved dramatically, allowing the practice to serve 15% more patients without extending hours.

Staff reported spending 75% less time on reminder calls, freeing them to focus on patient care and customer service. Perhaps most importantly, last-minute cancellations increased as patients who couldn't make appointments gave advance notice, allowing the practice to fill those slots from their waiting list.

"The ROI was clear within the first month," Dr. Chen notes. "But beyond the numbers, our patients appreciate the convenience, and our team is less stressed. It's been a win across the board."

# A Weekend in Porto: Portugal's Enchanting Second City

Just 2 hours and 50 minutes by train from Lisbon, Porto reveals itself as a city of timeless beauty and contemporary energy—perfect for an unforgettable weekend escape.

## Friday Evening: Ribeira's Golden Hour

Arrive in the afternoon and head straight to the Ribeira district along the Douro River. The colorful facades of medieval buildings glow in the evening light, creating an Instagram-worthy panorama. Settle into a riverside café for your first taste of *francesinha*, Porto's decadent sandwich layered with meats and drenched in beer sauce. As twilight falls, watch the Dom Luís I Bridge illuminate against the darkening sky.

## Saturday: Books, Tiles, and Port Wine

Start your morning at the magnificent Livraria Lello, one of the world's most beautiful bookstores. The 8-euro ticket is redeemable against any book purchase, making it well worth the price to climb the iconic red staircase and admire the stained-glass ceiling that inspired J.K. Rowling during her Porto years.

Next, visit São Bento Station to marvel at the 20,000 azulejo tiles depicting Portuguese history, then climb the Clérigos Tower for panoramic city views. In the afternoon, cross the bridge to Vila Nova de Gaia for port wine tastings. Graham's and Taylor's offer excellent tours with sweeping views back across the river.

## Sunday: Markets and Modernity

Spend Sunday morning exploring the Mercado do Bolhão, recently restored but retaining its authentic character. Sample local cheeses, fresh seafood, and *pastéis de nata* while chatting with vendors. Before departing, visit the contemporary Serralves Museum and its stunning gardens—a perfect contrast to the historic old town.

## Essential Tips

Porto's charm lies in its hills, so wear comfortable walking shoes. The Andante card provides unlimited public transport. Most importantly, don't rush—this is a city that rewards wanderers who get lost in its narrow streets and stumble upon hidden viewpoints.

Whether you're here for the architecture, the wine, or simply the atmosphere, Porto delivers a weekend that feels both authentic and magical—a city that proudly honors its past while embracing the present.

# A Weekend in Porto

Porto is about 2 hours 50 minutes from Lisbon by train, which makes it an easy weekend trip. It's hilly, a bit worn at the edges, and very good at being a city you wander around in.

## Friday evening: Ribeira

Get in by the afternoon and walk down to the Ribeira, the old district on the Douro. The medieval houses are painted every colour you can think of, and they look best around sunset. Grab a table at a café by the water and order a *francesinha*, the local sandwich: stacked meats, melted cheese, and a beer sauce poured over the top. It's heavy, so don't plan anything strenuous afterwards. When it gets dark, the Dom Luís I Bridge lights up, and it's worth lingering for.

## Saturday: books, tiles, port

Go to Livraria Lello first thing, before the queues build. The ticket is 8 euros, but you get it back if you buy a book, so you may as well. The red staircase and stained-glass ceiling are the draw. People like to say it inspired J.K. Rowling, who lived in Porto for a while, though the bookshop itself has played that story down.

After that, head to São Bento Station and look at the azulejo panels, around 20,000 tiles showing scenes from Portuguese history. Then climb the Clérigos Tower for the view over the rooftops. In the afternoon, cross the bridge to Vila Nova de Gaia and do a port tasting. Graham's and Taylor's both run good tours, and you can look back across the river at the city while you sip.

## Sunday: market and museum

Spend the morning at the Mercado do Bolhão. It was renovated recently but still feels like a real market. Buy some cheese, look at the seafood, eat a *pastel de nata*, and talk to the stallholders if your Portuguese or their English is up to it. Before you leave, go out to the Serralves Museum. The contemporary art is a change from the old town, and the gardens are lovely.

## A few tips

Wear comfortable shoes, because the hills are steep. The Andante card covers public transport, though you'll need to check which zones you need. And leave some slack in the schedule. Some of the best things in Porto are the viewpoints and little streets you find by taking a wrong turn.

# The Four-Day Week: Harbor Labs Shows Less Really Can Be More

When Harbor Labs announced their six-month trial of a four-day work week, skeptics predicted chaos. How could 24 staff members maintain productivity while working 20% fewer hours? The results tell a different story—output didn't just hold steady, it rose by 9%.

This isn't magic. It's what happens when companies recognize that exhausted employees aren't productive employees. The traditional five-day week is a relic from an era of factory floors and time clocks, not knowledge work that demands creativity and focus. Harbor Labs' experience suggests we've been measuring success all wrong.

The 9% productivity gain likely stems from several factors. When people know they have limited time, they prioritize ruthlessly. Meetings get shorter and more focused. Email marathons give way to decisive communication. The busywork that expands to fill available time suddenly has nowhere to hide. Workers return each Monday genuinely refreshed, not just slightly less depleted than Friday.

Critics worry about client expectations and competitive disadvantage, but Harbor Labs operated in the real world with real deadlines. Their trial succeeded not despite market pressures but within them. The question isn't whether businesses can afford a four-day week—it's whether they can afford not to explore it when competitors might gain a 9% efficiency advantage while simultaneously winning the war for talent.

Of course, this model won't translate perfectly everywhere. Emergency services, retail, and manufacturing face different constraints. But for the knowledge economy where Harbor Labs operates, the implications are profound. If a company can produce more with less time, the five-day week isn't just outdated—it's wasteful.

The real test comes next. Will Harbor Labs make this permanent? Will other companies follow? The six-month trial proved the concept works, but lasting cultural change requires courage. Companies that pioneered remote work before the pandemic reaped enormous advantages. The four-day week may be the next frontier where early movers gain decisive edge.

Harbor Labs has demonstrated that the emperor has no clothes. The question now is whether the rest of the business world is ready to admit it.

**San Francisco, CA – November 6, 2026** – Tidepool, the leading tide and surf forecast application trusted by coastal communities and water sports enthusiasts, today announced it has raised $8 million in Series A funding led by Bramble Capital. The investment will accelerate product development, expand the platform's forecasting capabilities, and grow the team as Tidepool continues to serve its rapidly growing user base.

Since launching two years ago, Tidepool has become an essential tool for surfers, fishermen, kayakers, and beachgoers seeking accurate, hyperlocal ocean conditions. The app now serves 30,000 weekly active users across coastal regions, delivering real-time tide predictions, wave forecasts, wind speeds, and water temperatures through an intuitive mobile experience.

"We built Tidepool because existing solutions were either too complex for casual users or lacked the granularity that serious water sports enthusiasts need," said Sarah Chen, CEO and co-founder of Tidepool. "This funding validates our vision of making ocean forecasting accessible to everyone, whether you're planning a family beach day or timing your dawn patrol surf session."

The platform differentiates itself through proprietary forecasting algorithms that combine NOAA data with local observation networks, delivering predictions accurate to specific beaches and surf breaks rather than broad coastal regions. Users can save favorite locations, receive push notifications for optimal conditions, and access historical data to identify patterns.

"Tidepool has achieved remarkable product-market fit in a niche that's both passionate and underserved," said Marcus Webb, Managing Partner at Bramble Capital. "The ocean recreation market represents billions in annual spending, yet most participants still rely on outdated tools. Tidepool's modern approach and loyal user base position them to become the category leader."

The Series A funding will support several key initiatives, including expanding coverage to international coastlines, integrating marine weather safety alerts, and developing community features that allow users to share real-time conditions. Tidepool also plans to introduce premium subscription tiers with advanced forecasting tools for professional users.

# Our Bags Are Going Compostable

At Ridgeway Coffee, we spend a lot of time thinking about what goes *into* the cup. Lately we've been thinking just as hard about what the coffee comes home in. So we're happy to announce that all of our retail bags are switching to compostable packaging.

## Why we're making the change

Ridgeway Coffee was founded in 2019 with a simple idea: great coffee should be sourced, roasted, and served with care. That care has always extended beyond flavor. But packaging has been a stubborn blind spot. Traditional coffee bags are usually made from layers of plastic and foil that are hard to recycle and almost always end up in a landfill.

Scale makes this matter. We now run 14 cafes and ship about 40,000 bags of coffee a year. Every one of those bags is a small decision, and 40,000 small decisions add up quickly. We wanted to make sure each one points in the right direction.

## What's changing

Our new bags are designed to break down in a commercial composting facility, turning back into soil instead of sitting in a landfill for decades. They're built to protect your beans just as well as before, with a one-way valve to let the roast gases escape and a seal that keeps oxygen and moisture out. You won't notice a difference in freshness. You'll just notice a different feel in your hands.

The switch applies to every retail bag, across all our cafes and our online shop, so there's no need to hunt for a special option. If you buy Ridgeway beans, you're getting the new packaging.

## How to dispose of your bag

Compostable doesn't mean it will vanish in your backyard bin. For best results:

- Empty the bag and give it a quick shake.
- Drop it in a commercial composting or green-waste bin where accepted.
- Check your local facility's guidelines if you're unsure.
- Don't put it in standard recycling, where it can cause contamination.

We'll also have a collection bin at each of our cafes, so you can bring empty bags back to us and we'll make sure they get composted properly.

## What's next

This is one step, not the finish line. We're continuing to look at our shipping boxes, cup lids, and café supplies, and we'll share what we learn along the way.

Thank you for drinking Ridgeway coffee, and for helping us make each bag count. Tell us what you think. We'd love your feedback.

*The Ridgeway Coffee Team*

Fiddle-leaf figs (*Ficus lyrata*) are famously particular, but repotting them doesn't have to be stressful. Done at the right time and in the right way, it gives the roots fresh room and keeps your plant growing strong. Follow these steps for a smooth transition.

## When to Repot

Plan to repot your fiddle-leaf fig **every 18 months**. Fresh soil replenishes nutrients, and a larger container prevents the plant from becoming root-bound. Signs it's time include roots poking out of the drainage holes, water running straight through the pot, or growth that has slowed noticeably.

The best season is **spring**. The plant is entering its active growing period, so it recovers quickly and establishes new roots with minimal setbacks.

## What You'll Need

- A new pot that is **2 inches wider** than the current one
- Well-draining potting mix (an aroid or indoor-plant blend works well)
- Gloves
- A small trowel
- A tray or saucer

## Step-by-Step Instructions

### 1. Choose the Right Pot

Select a container that is **2 inches wider** in diameter than the existing pot. Going much larger leaves excess soil that stays wet and invites root rot. Make sure the pot has **drainage holes**. Without them, water pools at the bottom and quickly damages the roots.

### 2. Prepare the Plant

Water your fig lightly a day before repotting. Slightly moist soil holds together better and makes removal easier.

### 3. Remove the Plant

Tip the pot gently on its side and slide the plant out, supporting the base of the trunk. If it's stuck, run a trowel around the inside edge or tap the sides of the pot.

### 4. Inspect the Roots

Loosen any tightly wound roots with your fingers. Trim away anything black, mushy, or foul-smelling with clean shears. Healthy roots are firm and pale.

### 5. Replant

Add a few inches of fresh mix to the new pot. Center the plant so the top of the root ball sits about an inch below the rim. Fill in around the sides, pressing the soil down lightly to remove air pockets.

### 6. Water and Settle

Water thoroughly until it drains from the bottom, then empty the saucer. Place the plant back in bright, indirect light.

## Aftercare

Avoid fertilizing for about four to six weeks while the roots settle. Some leaf drop is normal, but keep watering consistent and avoid moving the plant around. Within a few weeks, you should see healthy, steady growth.

# How to Repot a Fiddle-Leaf Fig

Fiddle-leaf figs (*Ficus lyrata*) have a reputation for being fussy, and it's mostly deserved. Repotting is one of the easier jobs, though. Pick a decent time, don't rush it, and the roots get room to spread out and the plant keeps growing.

## When to Repot

Plan on repotting about **every 18 months**. The old soil runs out of nutrients by then, and the plant tends to outgrow its pot. You'll know it's time if roots are poking out of the drainage holes, water runs straight through without soaking in, or growth has slowed down.

**Spring** is the best season. The plant is waking up and ready to grow, so it bounces back fast and settles into the new pot with little fuss.

## What You'll Need

- A new pot that is **2 inches wider** than the current one
- Well-draining potting mix (an aroid or indoor-plant blend works well)
- Gloves
- A small trowel
- Clean shears
- A tray or saucer

## Step-by-Step Instructions

### 1. Choose the Right Pot

Get a pot that is **2 inches wider** across than the one you have now. Don't go much bigger. All that extra soil stays wet for too long, and that's how you get root rot. The pot also needs **drainage holes**. Without them, water collects at the bottom and the roots suffer.

### 2. Prepare the Plant

Give the fig a light watering the day before. Soil that's a bit damp holds together, so the plant comes out more easily.

### 3. Remove the Plant

Lay the pot gently on its side and slide the plant out, holding the base of the trunk as you go. If it won't budge, run a trowel around the inside edge or tap the sides of the pot.

### 4. Inspect the Roots

Use your fingers to loosen any roots that are wound tightly. Cut off anything that's black, mushy, or smells bad, using clean shears. Healthy roots are firm and pale.

### 5. Replant

Put a few inches of fresh mix in the bottom of the new pot. Set the plant in the middle so the top of the root ball sits about an inch below the rim. Fill in around the sides and press the soil down lightly to push out air pockets.

### 6. Water and Settle

Water well, until it runs out the bottom, then empty the saucer. Put the plant back somewhere with bright, indirect light.

## Aftercare

Hold off on fertilizer for four to six weeks while the roots settle in. Losing a few leaves is normal. Keep the watering steady and try not to move the plant around. After a few weeks you should see steady new growth.

# Summer Reading Challenge Returns to Hollis Public Library

Last summer, 1,200 children in our community picked up a book and kept turning pages. This year, the Hollis Public Library is inviting even more young readers to join the fun when the Summer Reading Challenge returns on **June 15**. It will run for **8 weeks**.

## What Is the Challenge?

The Summer Reading Challenge is a free program for children of all ages and reading levels. The idea is simple: read throughout the summer, track your progress, and earn rewards along the way. Whether your child is just learning to sound out words, devouring chapter books, or happiest with a stack of comics, there is a place for them in this program.

## Why It Matters

Educators have long observed that children who stop reading over the summer can lose some of the skills they gained during the school year. Regular reading, even for a few minutes each day, helps keep those skills sharp. It also builds imagination, vocabulary, and confidence. Best of all, it can be a lot of fun.

## How It Works

- **Sign up at the library.** Stop by the children's desk any time on or after June 15 to register and pick up a reading log.
- **Read your way.** Picture books, audiobooks, graphic novels, and books read aloud with a family member all count.
- **Hit milestones.** Each week, readers can bring their logs to the desk to collect stickers and small prizes.
- **Celebrate together.** Throughout the eight weeks, look out for story times, craft afternoons, and special guests.

## Get Involved

Families can help by setting aside a regular reading time, visiting the library together each week, and letting children choose books that spark their curiosity. Our librarians are always happy to suggest titles for every interest, from dinosaurs and dragons to mysteries and space adventures.

Teens and adults are welcome too. Reading alongside your children is one of the best ways to show them that books are for everyone.

## Join Us

Last year's turnout of 1,200 children was something the whole community can be proud of. Let's make this summer even bigger. Mark your calendar for June 15, bring your library card, and get ready to read.

For more information, ask at the front desk or call the Hollis Public Library.

I'm thrilled to share some news: I've been promoted to **Head of Design at Northwind**! 🎉

Six years ago, I joined Northwind as a designer with a lot of curiosity and a very full sketchbook. I had no idea how much I'd grow here, or how many brilliant, generous people I'd get to learn from along the way. Today, I'm stepping into a role I once only dreamed about.

**Looking back**

Over the past six years, I've had the chance to:

- Ship products that I'm genuinely proud of
- Make plenty of mistakes, and learn more from them than from any success
- Work alongside people who challenged my thinking and made me better
- Watch design move from a "nice-to-have" to a true seat at the table

None of that happens alone. To my teammates, mentors, and cross-functional partners: thank you for your trust, your honest feedback, and your patience on the days when the prototype just wouldn't cooperate.

**Looking ahead**

In my new role, I'll be leading a team of 9 incredibly talented designers, researchers, and creatives. I'm honored by that responsibility, and I take it seriously. Leading a team isn't about having all the answers. It's about creating the conditions where great work can happen: clear direction, psychological safety, room to experiment, and a culture where everyone's voice shapes the outcome.

Here's what I'm committed to as we move forward:

1. **Craft with purpose.** Every pixel should serve a person, not just a screen.
2. **Collaboration over ego.** The best ideas come from the room, not from a title.
3. **Growth for everyone.** I want each person on this team to leave a project stronger than they entered it.
4. **Curiosity, always.** The moment we stop asking "why," we stop designing.

To the Northwind leadership team, thank you for believing in me and in the power of design. I can't wait to show you what we can build together.

And to my design team: I'm so excited to get started. Let's make something remarkable.

If you're passionate about design, leadership, or just want to say hello, I'd love to connect and hear your story too.

Here's to what's next. 🚀

You became a dentist to care for patients, not to chase receipts, reconcile accounts, or decode spreadsheets at 10 p.m. Toothbook handles your books so you can get back to what you do best.

**[Start Your Free Consultation](#)**

---

## Your books, closed within 48 hours

Most practices wait weeks after month end to see their numbers. By then, the information is stale and the decisions have already been made. Toothbook closes your books within **48 hours of month end**, so you always know where your practice stands while it still matters.

## Made for dentistry, not just any business

Dental finances are different. Insurance payments arrive late and in pieces. Lab fees, supply orders, and equipment financing all need careful tracking. Associate compensation, hygiene production, and collections each tell a different story.

Our bookkeepers work with dental practices every day. We know the difference between production and collections, and we set up your chart of accounts to reflect how your practice really runs.

- **A dedicated bookkeeper.** One person who knows your practice and your questions.
- **Tax-ready records.** Your accountant gets clean books, without the scramble in March.

## Simple, honest pricing

**$299 a month.**

One flat price. No setup fees, no hourly surprises, and no long-term contracts. Cancel whenever you like.

## How it works

1. **Connect your accounts.** Securely link your bank, credit cards, payroll, and practice management software.
2. **We get to work.** Your bookkeeper cleans up your records and sets up your dental-specific categories.
3. **Receive your books.** Each month, within 48 hours of month end, your reports arrive ready to review.

## Ready for books you can trust?

Join the 140 practices that have handed off the paperwork and gained back their evenings. Book a short call, and we'll show you exactly how Toothbook fits your practice.

# Kestrel 2: A Fast, Honest Daily Trainer

After 300 miles in the Kestrel 2, I feel confident saying this is one of the more dependable trainers I've worn at its price. It doesn't try to be everything, but what it does, it does well.

## First Impressions

Out of the box, the Kestrel 2 feels light and purposeful. It weighs 248 grams, which puts it comfortably below many daily trainers that creep toward the 300-gram mark. The upper is a breathable engineered mesh that wrapped my midfoot securely without any hot spots, even during the first run. The fit is true to size, with a roomy toe box that leaves space for swelling on longer efforts.

## On the Run

The Kestrel 2 has an 8 mm drop, a traditional geometry that suits heel strikers and midfoot runners alike. I found the transition smooth whether I was cruising at an easy pace or pushing through tempo intervals. The midsole foam is responsive without being harsh. It isn't the bounciest foam on the market, but it has a lively, stable feel that stayed consistent from the first mile to the last.

Over those 300 miles, I used the shoe for everything: recovery jogs, long runs up to 16 miles, and a few fartlek sessions. It handled all of it without complaint. Stability is solid for a neutral shoe, and I never felt wobbly on corners or uneven pavement.

## Durability

This is where the Kestrel 2 impressed me most. At 300 miles, the outsole rubber shows wear at the heel and under the forefoot, but nothing alarming. The midsole has lost a little of its initial pop, which is normal, yet it still offers adequate cushioning. The upper has no tears or fraying. I expect to squeeze another 50 to 100 miles from this pair as a walking or short-run shoe.

## Downsides

It isn't perfect. The tongue is slightly thin and can shift if you don't lace carefully. Wet-weather traction is merely average, so I'd be cautious on slick surfaces. And if you want a plush, max-cushioned ride, this isn't it.

## Verdict

At $140, the Kestrel 2 delivers excellent value. It's light, versatile, and durable, a shoe that rewards consistent training rather than flashy marketing. If you're looking for a single pair to handle most of your weekly mileage, this is an easy recommendation.

**Rating: 4.5 out of 5**

# Heat Pumps Explained: Are They Worth It?

## What is a heat pump?

A heat pump is an electric appliance that heats and cools your home by moving heat rather than creating it. In winter, it pulls heat from the outdoor air, even when it feels cold, and transfers it inside. In summer, it reverses direction and works like an air conditioner, pushing indoor heat outside. One machine does the job of both a furnace and an AC unit.

The key idea is that moving heat takes far less energy than generating it. A furnace burns fuel or runs electric resistance coils to make heat. A heat pump simply relocates warmth that already exists.

## How efficient is it?

This is where heat pumps shine. A good heat pump delivers about 300% efficiency, meaning it produces roughly three units of heat for every one unit of electricity it uses. Even the best gas furnaces top out below 100%, and electric baseboard heaters hit exactly 100%. That gap translates directly into lower energy bills for many households.

## Does it work in the cold?

Older models struggled in freezing weather, but technology has improved dramatically. Many models now work down to -15°C (5°F), making them viable in much of the country, including colder regions. Performance and efficiency do drop as temperatures fall, so it's worth choosing a cold-climate model and having your installer size the system properly. Some homes in very cold areas pair a heat pump with a backup heat source.

## How long does it last?

Expect a heat pump to last around 15 years with regular maintenance, such as cleaning filters and annual inspections. That's comparable to a typical air conditioner. Because it runs year-round for both heating and cooling, it may see more wear than a standalone AC, so upkeep matters.

## What does it cost?

Upfront costs are higher than a basic furnace or AC replacement, often several thousand dollars depending on your home, ductwork, and region. Help is available: the federal tax credit is up to $2,000, which can take a meaningful bite out of the bill. Check for additional state and utility rebates, which can stack on top.

## So, is it worth it?

For most people, yes, especially if:

- You're replacing an aging AC or furnace anyway
- You currently heat with electricity, oil, or propane
- You want to cut energy use and emissions
- Your local electricity rates are reasonable compared with gas

It may be a tougher sell if you have very cheap natural gas, an extremely cold climate, or a home that needs costly ductwork upgrades. Get quotes from several installers, factor in incentives, and compare estimated yearly energy costs. For many households, the efficiency savings and available credits make a heat pump a smart long-term investment.

# Fernhill Dental Cuts No-Shows by 11 Points with Text Reminders

## At a Glance

- **Customer:** Fernhill Dental
- **Locations:** 2 clinics
- **Challenge:** High rate of missed appointments
- **Solution:** Automated text message reminders
- **Result:** No-shows fell from 18% to 7% in 3 months

## The Challenge

For Fernhill Dental, an empty chair meant more than a gap in the schedule. Nearly one in five booked appointments ended in a no-show. Each missed visit meant lost revenue, idle staff time, and a patient who had not received the care they needed.

The team had tried phone call reminders, but the approach was slow and unreliable. Front desk staff spent hours each week leaving voicemails that were rarely returned, and that time was taken away from patients standing in the clinic. With an 18% no-show rate across both locations, the practice knew it needed a better way to stay in touch.

## The Solution

Fernhill Dental introduced automated text message reminders for every appointment at both clinics. Patients now receive a confirmation when they book, a reminder a few days before the visit, and a final nudge the day before. Each message lets patients confirm with a single reply or ask to reschedule.

Setup was quick, and the system fit into the practice's existing scheduling routine. Staff no longer needed to make reminder calls by hand, and any cancellations were visible right away, so the team could offer the open slot to someone on the waiting list.

## The Results

Within three months, the results were clear:

- **No-shows dropped from 18% to 7%** across both clinics
- **Fewer last-minute gaps**, as patients rescheduled in advance rather than not showing up
- **More front desk time** freed up for in-person patient care

"Patients respond to texts in minutes, not days," said a member of the Fernhill team. "We spend far less time chasing people and far more time looking after them."

The improvement was consistent at both locations, which suggests the approach works regardless of patient mix or clinic size.

## Looking Ahead

Encouraged by the results, Fernhill Dental plans to expand its use of text messaging to include post-visit follow-ups and recall reminders for routine cleanings. With a healthier schedule and a more engaged patient base, the practice is better positioned to grow while keeping the personal touch its patients value.

An 11-point drop in missed appointments shows how a simple, well-timed message can make a real difference for a busy dental practice.

## At a Glance

- **Customer:** Fernhill Dental
- **Locations:** 2 clinics
- **Challenge:** High rate of missed appointments
- **Solution:** Automated text message reminders
- **Result:** No-shows fell from 18% to 7% in 3 months

## The Challenge

Nearly one in five appointments at Fernhill Dental ended in a no-show. Every one of them cost the practice money and left staff with nothing to do. It also meant a patient went without care they needed.

The team had tried calling patients to remind them. It didn't work well. Front desk staff spent hours every week leaving voicemails that hardly anyone returned, and that was time they couldn't spend on the people standing right in front of them. At 18% across both clinics, the practice knew it had to find a better way to reach people.

## The Solution

Fernhill started sending automated text reminders for every appointment at both clinics. A patient gets a confirmation when they book, a reminder a few days out, and one more the day before. They can confirm by replying once, or ask to reschedule.

Setup was quick, and it slotted into the way the practice already handled scheduling. Staff stopped making reminder calls by hand. Cancellations also showed up right away, so the team could offer the empty slot to someone on the waiting list.

## The Results

Three months in, the numbers spoke for themselves:

- **No-shows dropped from 18% to 7%** across both clinics
- **Fewer last-minute gaps**, because patients rescheduled ahead of time instead of simply not turning up
- **More front desk time** for patients who are actually in the clinic

"Patients answer a text in minutes, not days," said a member of the Fernhill team. "We spend far less time chasing people and far more time looking after them."

Both locations saw the same improvement, which suggests it doesn't depend on the clinic's size or who its patients are.

## Looking Ahead

Fernhill plans to do more with text messaging, starting with post-visit follow-ups and recall reminders for routine cleanings. A fuller schedule and patients who are paying closer attention leave the practice room to grow without losing the personal touch its patients like.

An 11-point drop in missed appointments shows what a short message, sent at the right time, can do for a busy dental practice.

# A Weekend in Porto: Tiles, Port, and River Light

Porto has a way of slowing you down. Steep cobbled lanes, laundry fluttering from balconies, and the smell of grilled sardines drifting up from the Douro make it a city best explored on foot, with no strict plan. Here's how I spent a perfect weekend there.

## Getting There

I started in Lisbon, and the train couldn't have been easier. The journey takes **2 hours 50 minutes**, which gave me just enough time to watch the countryside roll by, finish a coffee, and read half a novel. Arriving at São Bento station is an event in itself. Its main hall is covered in more than 20,000 blue-and-white azulejo tiles depicting scenes from Portuguese history.

## Saturday: Books and Bridges

Start the day at **Livraria Lello**, one of the world's most beautiful bookshops. The **ticket costs 8 euros**, and it's worth every cent. The sweeping red staircase and carved wooden ceilings feel like something out of a fairy tale. Arrive early, as lines build quickly by mid-morning.

From there, wander down toward the Ribeira district. Cross the double-decker Dom Luís I Bridge on foot and take in the view of the terracotta rooftops tumbling toward the river. For lunch, order a *francesinha*, the city's famous sandwich stacked with meats, covered in melted cheese, and drowned in a spicy beer sauce. It's gloriously excessive.

In the afternoon, cross to Vila Nova de Gaia and visit one of the port wine cellars. A tasting of tawny and ruby ports is the ideal way to spend a lazy hour or two. Stay for sunset on the riverbank, when the whole waterfront glows gold.

## Sunday: Slow Mornings

Begin with a *pastel de nata* and a strong *bica* at a neighborhood café. Then stroll through the Jardins do Palácio de Cristal, where peacocks roam freely and the views over the river are hard to beat. If you have energy left, browse the boutiques and street art around Rua de Miguel Bombarda.

## Final Thoughts

Porto is compact, friendly, and deeply atmospheric. Two days won't be enough, but they'll be enough to make you plan your return. Pack comfortable shoes, bring an appetite, and leave room in your suitcase for a bottle of port.

# A Weekend in Porto: Tiles, Port, and River Light

Porto slows you down whether you want it to or not. The lanes are steep and cobbled, laundry hangs off the balconies, and grilled sardines smell up the whole street near the Douro. I didn't bring much of a plan, and I'd say that was the right call. This is how my weekend went.

## Getting There

I came up from Lisbon by train. It takes **2 hours 50 minutes**, which was just long enough for a coffee, a lot of staring out the window, and about half a novel. Then you walk into São Bento station and forget about the book. The main hall is covered floor to ceiling in more than 20,000 blue-and-white azulejo tiles showing scenes from Portuguese history. I stood there far longer than I'd meant to.

## Saturday: Books and Bridges

First stop was **Livraria Lello**, often called one of the most beautiful bookshops in the world. The **ticket is 8 euros**, and I didn't mind paying. The red staircase curls up through carved wooden ceilings and the whole place feels a bit like a storybook. Go early. By mid-morning the line is long.

After that I drifted downhill to the Ribeira and walked across the double-decker Dom Luís I Bridge. The terracotta rooftops spill down to the river, and I stopped halfway to take it in. Lunch was a *francesinha*, Porto's famous sandwich: meats piled high, smothered in melted cheese, then drenched in a spicy beer sauce. It's absurd, and I'd order it again.

In the afternoon I crossed into Vila Nova de Gaia and visited a port cellar. I tried a tawny and a ruby and let an hour or two slip by. We stayed on the riverbank for sunset, when the whole waterfront turns gold.

## Sunday: Slow Mornings

Sunday started with a *pastel de nata* and a strong *bica* at a café near where I was staying. Then I wandered through the Jardins do Palácio de Cristal, where peacocks stroll around like they own the place and the river views are lovely. If you still have some energy, the boutiques and street art around Rua de Miguel Bombarda are worth a look.

## Final Thoughts

Porto is small, friendly, and full of atmosphere. Two days isn't enough, but it was plenty to make me start planning a return. Wear comfortable shoes, come hungry, and save room in your suitcase for a bottle of port.

# Four Days Is Not a Perk. It's a Strategy.

For decades, we've treated the five-day week as a law of nature. It isn't. It's a habit, inherited from factory floors and defended mostly by people who have never measured whether it works.

Harbor Labs did measure. Over six months, the company ran a four-day week trial with 24 staff. At the end, output had risen 9%. Not held steady. Not "only dipped slightly." Risen.

Skeptics will say 24 people is a small sample, and they're right. This is not a peer-reviewed study of the global economy. But a small trial is exactly what a sensible company should run before changing how it operates. It is cheap, it is reversible, and it produces evidence rather than opinions. The more interesting question is why anyone would be surprised by the result.

Most of us know how a typical Wednesday goes. A meeting that could have been an email. A status update about a status update. An afternoon spent looking busy because leaving would look lazy. When you take away a fifth of the week, something has to give, and what gives is the waste. People decline pointless meetings. They protect their focus. They get on with the work because they have a reason to: Friday is theirs.

That is the real lesson. The four-day week works not because people secretly have an extra day of productivity hidden in them, but because scarcity sharpens attention. Give someone less time and a clear goal, and they will often find a smarter route.

There is a human argument too, and it shouldn't be dismissed as soft. Rested people make fewer mistakes, stay longer, and don't spend their evenings quietly updating their résumés. Retention is a cost. Burnout is a cost. A longer weekend is, among other things, a cheap way to reduce both.

None of this means every business can copy Harbor Labs tomorrow. Hospitals, shops and support desks face real scheduling constraints. But "it's complicated" is a reason to design carefully, not a reason to refuse to look.

If a company can do 9% more with a day less, the burden of proof has shifted. It's now the five-day week that needs to justify itself.

# Tidepool Raises $8 Million Series A to Help More People Read the Water

Today we're thrilled to announce that Tidepool has raised an $8 million Series A, led by Bramble Capital. The funding will help us build the most trusted tide and surf forecast app for everyone who lives, works, or plays by the coast.

## Why we started Tidepool

Anyone who has driven an hour to the beach only to find a blown-out, closed-out mess knows the frustration. Conditions on the coast change quickly, and the information to predict them is scattered across buoy readings, tide tables, wind models, and local knowledge. We built Tidepool to bring all of it together in one clear, honest forecast.

## Where we are today

Tidepool now has 30,000 weekly users, including surfers, anglers, paddleboarders, tide-poolers, kayakers, and families planning a day at the shore. Most of that growth has come from word of mouth, which is the best compliment we could ask for. People tell their friends because the forecasts help them make better decisions, whether that means catching the right swell window or avoiding a high tide at a tricky launch.

## What the funding makes possible

With Bramble Capital's support, we're focusing on three priorities:

- **Better forecasts.** We're investing in improved wave and tide modeling, with finer detail for more breaks and beaches.
- **Smarter alerts.** You'll be able to set personal conditions, such as swell size, wind direction, and tide height, and get notified the moment they line up.
- **A stronger team.** We're hiring engineers, data scientists, and designers who care about the ocean as much as we do.

## A note of thanks

"Bramble Capital understood right away that this is about more than numbers on a screen," our team likes to say. "It's about getting people outside, safely, at the right time." We're grateful to them for believing in that mission, and to our early users for shaping the product with every piece of feedback.

The ocean doesn't keep a schedule, but with the right information, you can. We're just getting started, and we can't wait to show you what's next.

See you at the water.

**The Tidepool Team**
